messages.author: 27daa73cdb503da4
messages.subject: Non-centered, censored data
parts:
Hi all,

Ben Goodrich was kind enough to show me how to model censored multivariate data, but I'm having trouble converting things to a non-centered parameterisation.
Moving from y_c ~ multi_normal_cholesky_lpdf(mu, L_Sigma) to the model below results in divergent transitions with every iteration (ie. n_divergent = n_iter) and low BFMI warnings for all chains. 

Is there something obvious that I've missed?

Thanks for your help,
Andrew

data {
  vector[S] y[N];    // Data
  vector[S] mu[N];
  int<lower=0> N;    // Number of observations
  int<lower=2> S;     // Number of dimensions 
  int<lower=0> n_censored;     // Number of censored observations
  int<lower=0> is_censored[n_censored, 2];     // Positions of censored observations
}
parameters {
  cholesky_factor_corr[S] L_Omega;
  vector<lower=0>[S] sigma;
  vector[S] alpha;
  vector<upper=0>[n_censored] y_miss;
}
transformed parameters{
  vector[S] y_c[N];
  y_c = y;
  for(i in 1:n_censored){
    y_c[is_censored[i, 1], is_censored[i, 2]] = y_miss[i];
  }
  for(i in 1:N) {
    y_c[i] = mu[i] + sigma .* (L_Omega * alpha);
  }
}
model {
  //Priors
  L_Omega ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(2);
  sigma ~ cauchy(0, 5);
  alpha ~ normal(0, 1);
}

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Non-centered, censored data
parts:
Shouldn't there be a distribution for y in there somewhere?
From what I can see, the y_miss get improper priors, do not
show up in the likelihood, and so will get an improper posterior.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Non-centered, censored data
parts:
Also, you don't want to do this:

y_c = y;

That'll just throw a bunch of variables on the autodiff stack
that you then throw away by reassignment.

- Bob

Ok, thanks - I'll add the uncensored data piecemeal to avoid reassigning.

In the centered version y_c ~ multi_normal_cholesky_lpdf(mu, L_Sigma) my understanding was that y_miss were drawn from the same distribution as y_c, similar to example 11.3 in the manual.

Is this not the case in the non-centered parameterisation?

Thanks for your help,
Andrew
